topic: Slate Auto launches affordable EV truck
headline: Slate Auto's $24,950 EV truck starts at $24,950
summary: Slate Auto's electric truck starts at $24,950, with a range of 205 miles.
details: Slate Auto, backed by billionaire Jeff Bezos, has revealed the starting price of its electric truck: $24,950. The company started taking pre-orders for the truck on Wednesday.
The base model has an estimated range of 205 miles, up from the initially estimated 150 miles. The SUV version of the truck will start at $29,950.

The truck has hand-crank windows, lacks an infotainment system, and all orders start with the same gray composite material, with no paint options. Slate plans to let buyers order customizable wraps for the vehicle.
Slate has said it 'won’t have traditional dealerships,' and plans to sell directly to customers, similar to other EV companies like Tesla, Rivian, and Lucid Motors.
caption:
Can a $24,950 electric truck disrupt the market?

Slate Auto, backed by billionaire Jeff Bezos, has revealed the starting price of its electric truck: $24,950. The company started taking pre-orders for the truck on Wednesday.

The base model has an estimated range of 205 miles, up from the initially estimated 150 miles. The SUV version of the truck will start at $29,950.

The truck has hand-crank windows, lacks an infotainment system, and all orders start with the same gray composite material, with no paint options. Slate plans to let buyers order customizable wraps for the vehicle.

Slate has said it 'won’t have traditional dealerships,' and plans to sell directly to customers, similar to other EV companies like Tesla, Rivian, and Lucid Motors.

headline_marked: Qualcomm Buys Chip Startup Modular for [[Nearly $4 Billion]]
headline: Qualcomm Buys Chip Startup Modular for Nearly $4 Billion
summary: Qualcomm acquires Modular, a Silicon Valley chip startup, for nearly $4 billion. The deal includes $300 million for Modular employees.
details: Qualcomm will acquire the Silicon Valley chip startup Modular for nearly $4 billion. The companies announced the acquisition on Wednesday; Qualcomm said it expects to issue up to 19.2 million shares of common stock in the deal, which works out to just under $4 billion based on the company's last closing share price.

The deal, which includes $300 million for Modular employees, comes nine months after the chip startup raised $250 million at a $1.6 billion valuation . It’s expected to close in the second half of this year.

Modular makes and sells a chip software platform. It also produces a proprietary coding language that allows developers to write AI software to run on different chips without having to rewrite the code for each chip.

The startup’s entire team, which includes its two cofounders and around 150 employees, are expected to join Qualcomm. “We believe the future belongs to developer-friendly, horizontal platforms that can run across diverse compute environments and give customers real choice in how and where they deploy AI,” said Qualcomm president and CEO Cristiano Amon in a statement .
